analysis:
Examined both workflow excerpts, the changelog's metadata/patch/source, and the build documentation's metadata/patch against the indexed model and selected detailed evidence. No supported security regression was identified. The workflow switches to release toolchain mode (changed-range context at .github/workflows/release-provider.yml:112–114) and updates the older-macOS validation's required SDK from 27.0 to 27.2 (head:1444), without weakening its source, bundle-digest, signature, stapling or runtime-smoke checks (1438–1464). Surrounding release behavior retains hardened signing, helper-specific identities, entitlement checks, final artifact hashes/full CodeDirectory identity, and separate staging/publication jobs (658–760, 939–998, 1184–1405). These bear on A-011, A-017, T-013, T-034 and T-054; publication remains distinct from independent qualification under TB-011. No changes to inference encryption, cache isolation/storage (T-041), billing, token revocation or local hold controls are evidenced here.
Documentation at docs/developer/build.md:162–184 and changelog.d/ci-xcode-27-2-toolchain.md:3–7 describes strict release SDK/Swift versions but a broader default qualification mode. Integration must verify scripts/prepare-provider-release-toolchain.sh and scripts/provider-release-swift.sh enforce those modes, propagate the selected SDK/DEVELOPER_DIR consistently, and reject incompatible resumed unsigned builds. Also reconcile the mode settings in the other changed CI/signing/qualification workflows and mise.toml. Those implementations are outside these units, so the documented contracts are not proof of enforcement or a missing control. Remaining uncertainty concerns release/qualification provenance consistency, not evidence of an authorization bypass; unchanged external coordinator implementations need not be re-audited for this toolchain change.
